title: ChatGPT assists a literature review of MRI features of intravascular lymphoma after biopsy diagnosis
summary: Chinese neurologists used ChatGPT to help review published MRI findings of cerebral intravascular large B-cell lymphoma for a 59-year-old's case report; the diagnosis came from biopsy, not the model.
account: Chen et al. (Frontiers in Immunology, 14 November 2024), from the Affiliated Yuebei People's Hospital of Shantou University Medical College in Shaoguan, report a previously healthy 59-year-old woman who developed hemiparesis and altered mental status after SARS-CoV-2 reinfection, was first treated for presumed infarction and then for suspected demyelination, and was diagnosed with intravascular large B-cell lymphoma by brain biopsy. The authors state that they reviewed the brain MRI findings of the disease in the literature 'with the assistance of ChatGPT' and describe their review as the first to focus on MRI features of cerebral lesions. The model played no part in the diagnosis or treatment; the earlier verifier set the case aside for that reason. The authors declare no competing interests. The date is the publication date.
purpose: Assist clinicians in reviewing published imaging literature for a case report
deployer: Affiliated Yuebei People's Hospital of Shantou University Medical College
taxonomy_note: The only AI role is literature-review assistance after a biopsy-confirmed diagnosis; no effect on the patient's care is claimed, so this is a general benefit with all depths null, kept under the no-discard rule.

ratings.reason: The model did not contribute to diagnosis or treatment.

ai_role.statement: ChatGPT assisted the authors' literature review for the published case; the patient's diagnosis and care did not involve the model. Source is a non-vendor peer-reviewed case report.
